items.title: '살아나나 했는데'…주력 SUV 부진에 KGM·르노·GM 하반기 고전

items.title: 미래에셋증권, 3분기 누적 순이익 2.5조…자사주 1.4조 소각키로

items.title: 한화 '오스탈USA' 인수 급물살…"협상 실질적 진전"
items.snippet: 한화그룹이 호주 조선 업체 오스탈(Austal)의 미국 사업 인수에 어느 때보다 가까이 다가갔다.오스탈은 최근 한화디펜스USA가 경쟁사인 미국의 와일드캣인프라스트럭쳐보다 오스탈과의 인수 협상에서 실질적으로 더 앞서 있다고 밝혔다. 미국 국방부(전쟁부) 역시 한화의 오스탈USA 인수를 지지하는 것으로 알려졌다.12일 외신과 업계에 따르면 한화그룹의 오스탈USA 인수 협상은 현재 구속적인 거래계약서를 논의하는 단계까지 진전된 상태다.한화는 지난 8월 미국 방산 자회사 한화디펜스USA를 통해 오스탈USA 인수를 위한 10억5천만~12억

items.title: CJ프레시웨이, B2B 실온 소스 매출 36% 증가…R&D확대 성과
items.snippet: CJ프레시웨이[051500]가 B2B(기업 간 거래) 실온 소스 연구개발을 확대하며 관련 매출 성장세를 뒷받침한다.CJ프레시웨이는 올해 1~3분기 실온 소스 PB(자체 브랜드) 상품 매출이 전년 동기 대비 36% 증가했다고 12일 밝혔다.CJ프레시웨이는 이 같은 매출 성장세를 지원하기 위해 상품 기획부터 배합 설계, 제조 공정, 품질 관리를 아우르는 통합 개발 역량을 바탕으로 B2B 실온 소스 연구개발을 확대하고 있다고 강조했다.실온 상품은 냉장 보관이나 별도 해동 과정이 필요하지 않아 사업장의 보관·조리 편의성을 높일 수 있다.

items.title: 한병도 “당청 엇박자 없다…더 나은 민생 위해 긴밀히 협력”
items.snippet: 한병도 더불어민주당 원내대표는 12일 “당·청 간 엇박자는 없다”며 “더 나은 민생을 위해 당과 정부가 긴밀히 협력하고 있다는 말씀을 확실히 드린다”고 강조했다.한 원내대표는 이날 국회에서 열린 정책조정회의에서 전날 이재명 대통령 초청으로 열린 당 지도부 만찬을 언급하며 이같이 말했다. 그는 “당은 양극화 극복과 소비 진작을 위해 정부의 과감하고 신속한 대책이 필요하다고 요청 드렸고, 대통령께서도 공감하시면서 한마음 한뜻으로 당·청이 움직여야 한다는 점을 강조하셨다”고 전했다.이어 “국민의힘이 정쟁에 매달릴 때 민주당과 이재명 정부는 민생에 매달리겠다”며 “국정과제와 민생입법에 속도를 내고 내년도 예산안도 법정 시한 안에 책임지고 처리하겠다”고 말했다. 그러면서 “오직 민생, 오직 국민만 바라보며 남은 정기국회에 총력을 다하겠다”고 덧붙였다....

items.snippet: 이용철 법무부 장관 후보자가 11일 이재명 대통령이 기소된 사건의 공소 취소 지휘 여부에 대해 “(조작기소 특검의) 진상 규명이 시작되지도 않았는데 예측, 예단과 억측을 전제로 한 논란에 의견을 드리는 건 적절치 않다”고 밝혔다. 이 후보자는 이날 서울 송파구 인사청문준비단 사무실로 첫 출근을 하며 공소 취소를 지휘할 것인지 묻는 질문에 “기존 입장에 변화는 없다”면서도 이같이 답했다. 이틀 전 이 후보자는 공소 취소 여부에 대해 “진상 규명에 집중하는 게 맞다”며 “나머지 일은 법과 원칙에 따라 하는 것이 바람직하다”고 첫 공식 입장을 밝혔다. 이를 놓고 야당에서 “공소 취소를 위한 수순”이라는 비판이 쏟아지자 이 후보자는 이날 “앞으로 특검의 진상 규명 활동에 대해 어떠한 예단과 선입견 없이 지켜보겠다”며 수위 조절에 나섰다.● 메모지에...

items.title: 조정식, 조작기소 특검법 논란에 “법적문제 없다”
items.snippet: 조정식 국회의장(사진)이 더불어민주당 주도로 국회 본회의를 통과한 조작수사·조작기소 진상규명 특검법’(조작기소 특검법) 위헌 논란에 대해 11일 “법적으로는 문제가 없다”고 정면으로 반박했다. 법안 통과 이후에도 야권을 중심으로 제기되는 ‘이재명 대통령 공소취소용 특검’이란 논란에 선을 긋고 나선 것. 조 의장은 이날 서울 중구 한국프레스센터에서 열린 관훈토론회에서 “9월 검찰개혁법을 처리하면서 그와 관계된 형사소송법을 여야가 같이 처리했는데, 부칙에 보면 파견 검사에 대해 수사권이 부여될 수 있다고 돼 있다”며 이같이 밝혔다. 이 대통령이 자신과 관련된 사건을 수사하는 특검을 임명하는 것은 이해충돌이라는 비판에 대해서도 “대통령 본인의 권한으로 보면 대법관이나 대법원장, 헌법재판소 소장 등 국가의 중요한 임명권을 법적으로 갖고 있지 않느냐”...

items.title: 정부 이어 여야도 코인 과세 2년 유예 잠정 합의
items.snippet: 여야가 11일 가상자산 소득과세 유예에 잠정적으로 합의했다. 이에 따라 내년 1월 시행 예정이던 가상자산 소득 과세는 2029년까지 2년간 유예된다. 국회 재정경제기획위원회 여당 간사인 더불어민주당 오기형 의원은 이날 국회에서 조세소위를 마친 뒤 기자들과 만나 “가상자산 (과세) 연기에 대한 공감대가 있었다”며 “정부에서는 (과세를) 2년 미루겠다고 했고 여야 간에도 별다른 이견이 없었다”고 전했다. 야당 간사인 국민의힘 배준영 의원도 “가상자산 과세는 벌써 세 차례 미뤘고, 2029년까지 미루면 네 차례가 된다”며 “정부가 연기해야 된다고 해서 결국 오늘 연기가 됐다”고 했다. 이어 “(과세를) 연기하는 만큼 앞으로 정부에서 책임 있게 준비해야 한다”며 “국회 차원에서도 준비가 어떻게 되고 있는지 면밀히 살피고 같이 지도해나갈 것”이라고 밝...

items.title: 靑 일축에도… 與 수도권의원 모임 토론회선 “비거주 규제 완화”
items.snippet: 더불어민주당 수도권 의원 20명이 소속된 ‘전월세 주거 안정화를 위한 부동산 실용주의 의원 모임(전실모)’ 첫 토론회에서 “노년층의 비거주에 대해 규제 예외 확대가 필요하다”는 주장이 나왔다. 1주택자 종합부동산세(종부세) 기본공제 통일 요구에 이어 비거주 규제 완화 필요성을 공식 제기한 것. 청와대가 거주용 주택에 대한 우대 원칙을 변경하는 건 불가하다는 입장을 고수하고 당 원내지도부도 개별 의견 표명 자제를 요청했음에도 수도권 의원들을 중심으로 부동산 세제 완화 요구가 확대되고 있는 것이다.● 종부세 기본공제 통일 이어 “비거주 규제 예외 확대” 요구 11일 국회 의원회관에서 열린 전실모의 첫 토론회에선 ‘전월세 가격 안정화를 위한 비거주 1주택 규제 재검토’를 주제로 부동산 세제 완화를 요구하는 목소리가 나왔다. 이언주 의원은 모두발언에...

items.title: 李, 與 투톱과 만찬 “당정 한뜻으로 움직여야”
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 11일 더불어민주당 투톱인 김민석 대표와 한병도 원내대표를 청와대로 초청해 만찬을 가졌다. 이 대통령은 이날 만찬에서 “우리 국민의 삶이 나아질 수 있도록 당정이 한마음 한뜻으로 움직여야 한다”며 내년도 예산안에 대한 여당과 국회의 적극적인 협조를 주문했다고 강유정 청와대 수석대변인이 서면 브리핑에서 전했다. 김 대표가 “양극화 극복과 소비 진작을 위해 정부의 과감하고 신속한 대책이 필요하다”고 요청하자 당정이 민생 의제에 집중하자는 당부를 한 것으로 풀이된다. 이날 만찬은 오후 6시 반부터 9시 20분까지 약 3시간 동안 이어졌다. 민주당 일각에서 종합부동산세(종부세) 기본공제 14억 원 통일 등 부동산 세제 완화 요구가 나온 것과 관련해선 별다른 논의가 이뤄지지 않은 것으로 알려졌다. 당내 일각의 요구와 관련해 당정 협의...

items.title: 北, ‘두 국가’ 헌법 공개… ‘남쪽 대한민국과 접경’ 못 박아
items.snippet: 북한이 11일 남한과의 ‘적대적 두 국가론’과 김정은 국무위원장의 핵무력 사용 권한을 명시한 헌법 개정안을 공개했다. 올 3월 헌법 개정 이후 8개월 만이자 2024년 3월 기존 헌법을 비공개 처리한 이후 2년 8개월 만에 외부에 헌법 조문을 공개한 것이다. 북한은 이날 온라인 선전매체 ‘내나라’에 3월 22, 23일 최고인민회의에서 개정한 168개조 분량의 헌법을 전격 공개했다. 새 헌법 2조에는 북한의 영토를 ‘북쪽으로 중국과 러시아, 남쪽으로 대한민국과 접하고 있는 영토와 그에 기초하여 설정된 영해와 영공’이라는 조항이 추가됐다. 또한 ‘북반부’라는 표현과 ‘자주 평화통일 민족대단결의 원칙에서 조국통일을 실현’한다는 조항도 삭제됐다. 이는 김 위원장이 2023년 12월 남북관계를 한민족이 아닌 적대적 두 국가로 규정한 것을 올 3월 개정...

items.title: 조현, 우크라 외교 만나 “성실한 합의 이행을”
items.snippet: 한국과 우크라이나 외교장관이 프랑스 파리에서 주요 7개국(G7) 외교장관회의를 계기로 대면 회담을 가졌다. 양국 장관이 직접 만난 것은 우크라이나의 북한군 포로 한국행 공개 이후 벌어진 양국 간 갈등 이후 처음이다. 11일 외교부에 따르면 조현 외교부 장관(사진)은 10일(현지 시간) 안드리 시비하 우크라이나 외교장관과 만나 국가 간 상호 존중 및 신뢰와 성실한 합의 이행을 강조하면서 현안이 원만히 해결되길 바란다고 말했다. 우크라이나가 북한군 포로의 한국행에 관한 비공개 합의를 어긴 데 대해 한국 정부가 요구해온 사과와 재발 방지 조치를 염두에 둔 발언으로 풀이된다. 시비하 장관은 양국 관계를 안정적으로 관리하고 발전시키기 위한 외교적 노력을 지속해 나가자고 밝혔지만 사과 요구나 재발 방지 대책에 대해선 언급하지 않았다. 다만 시비하 장관은...

items.title: 광주, 청년이 정책 만드는 ‘청년결정 정부’ 추진
items.snippet: 전남광주통합특별시는 10일 청년이 정책의 제안부터 결정·실행·평가까지 주체적으로 참여하는 청년결정 정부의 운영체계를 구체화하기 위해 자문회의를 열고 추진 방안을 논의했다고 11일 밝혔다. 자문회의는 청년결정 정부 구축·운영계획안을 공유하고 실질적 정책 참여와 의사결정 구조 마련을 위해 마련됐다. 청년결정 정부는 청년을 정책의 수혜자에서 주체로 전환해 정책 의제를 발굴·제안하고 결정과 실행 과정에 참여하도록 하는 청년 자치 모델이다. 광주특별시는 이를 위해 청년공회, 청년기획위원회, 전담 사무국을 중심으로 운영체계를 구축할 계획이다. 핵심 참여기구인 청년공회는 전남광주 거주 청년 50여 명으로 구성한다. 청년공회는 신규 청년정책 제안과 기존 정책의 개선 사항을 발굴하고 제안된 정책에 대한 숙의·의사결정·성과평가 등을 맡는다. 청년기획위원회는 분...

items.title: 유엔 참전용사를 향한 ‘감사의 빛’
items.snippet: 11일 밤 서울 광화문광장 ‘감사의 정원’에서 23줄기 푸른빛이 하늘로 치솟았다. 제20회 유엔 참전용사 국제추모의 날을 맞아서다. 매년 11월 11일은 6·25전쟁에 참전한 유엔군 용사들을 기리는 날이다. 2020년 법정 기념일로 지정됐다. 23줄기 빛은 우리나라와 6·25전쟁에 참전한 22국을 상징한다. 감사의 정원은 6·25전쟁 참전국의 희생과 헌신을 기리기 위해 지난 5월 개장했다. 높이 6.25m짜리 돌기둥 23개가 남북으로 나란히 늘어서 있다. 한 시민이 조형물 위에 LED 초를 올려놓으며 참전용사들을 추모하고 있다.

items.snippet: 지난 6일 더불어민주당 주도로 국회 본회의를 통과한 ‘조작기소 특검법’에 따라, 조만간 출범할 특검은 이재명 대통령이 기소된 사건 8건을 검찰이 수사·기소하는 과정에서 위법이 있었는지를 수사한다. 그런데 8건 중 3건은 하급심에서 이 대통령이나 공범, 관련 피고인에 대해 유죄 판단이 나왔고, 다른 2건은 대법원에서 유죄가 확정됐다. 법조계에선 “하급심에서 유죄 판결이 나왔거나 유죄가 확정된 사건까지 특검을 통해 뒤집으려는 것 아니냐”는 말이 나온다.

items.title: 이용철, 과거 ‘일가족 4명 살인범’ 변호 논란
items.snippet: 이용철 법무부 장관 후보자가 과거 ‘경기 양평 통나무집 일가족 살인 사건’ 상고심에서 피고인 측 변호인단에 이름을 올렸던 것으로 11일 확인됐다. 이 사건은 2002년 3월 25일 정모(당시 45세)씨가 양평군 옥천면 통나무집에서 지인 A씨와 A씨 아내, 두 자녀를 살해하고 불을 질러 시신을 훼손한 사건이다. 정씨는 사기 행각이 발각될까 두려워 A씨 일가족을 살해한 것으로 조사됐다. 정씨는 1심과 2심에서 사형을 선고받고 대법원에 상고했다. 정씨의 상고심 변호는 법무법인 새길이 맡았다. 당시 새길 대표변호사로 있던 이 후보자도 정씨 변호인단에 이름을 올렸다. 당시 정씨 변호인단은 “수사 과정에서 자백을 강요당했다”고 주장한 것으로 알려졌다. 그러나 대법원은 “같이 수감 생활을 한 이들의 진술에 따르면, 정씨가 구타나 고문을 당했거나, 가혹행위...

items.title: AMD, 6세대 에픽 '베니스' 공식 출시..."엔비디아 대비 성능 3.7배"
items.snippet: AMD가 6세대 서버용 중앙처리장치(CPU) 에픽 '베니스'를 공식 출시했다. 경쟁사 보다 높은 가격 대비 성능 효율(가성비)을 앞세워 시장 점유율을 확대한다.AMD는 10일(현지시간) Zen 6 마이크로아키텍처 기반 6세대 에픽의 주요 정보를 공개했다. 지난 1월 리사 수 최고경영자(CEO)가 CES 2026 기조연설 무대에서 실물 칩(실리콘)을 깜짝 공개한지 10개월 만이다.6세대 에픽 코드명은 베니스다. 현재 정식 판매에 돌입했으며 주요 서버 제조사들도 베니스 기반 시스템 출하를 시작했다. 마이크로소프트 애저와 오라클 클라우드

items.title: ‘양평고속도로 특혜’ 의혹 서기관 “특검 강압 수사로 잘못된 진술”
items.snippet: 최근 국토교통부의 ‘양평고속도로 종점 변경 특혜 의혹’ 사건 재판에서 핵심 피고인이 “민중기 특별검사팀의 강압수사로 조사 당시 잘못된 진술을 했다”고 했다. 지난 9일 이 사건을 심리중인 서울중앙지법 형사31부(재판장 박준석) 재판에서 국토부 김모 서기관은 “대통령직인수위원회 관계자로부터 고속도로 종점 변경을 검토하라는 연락을 받은 적이 없다”면서 종전 진술을 번복했다. 김 서기관은 특검 조사 때 “2022년 3월 인수위에 파견 나간 국토부 A 과장으로부터 ‘고속도로 종점 변경을 검토하라’는 지시를 받았다”고 했는데, 이 진술을 정반대로 뒤집은 것이다.

items.title: “취직 안하냐” 부모 잔소리에… 40대 캥거루족은 주먹 휘둘렀다
items.snippet: 지난 7월 강원 춘천시에서 A(43)씨가 아버지에게 주먹을 휘둘렀다. 부모와 함께 살던 A씨는 “술 좀 그만 마시고 취업하라”고 타이르는 아버지 얼굴을 때렸다. A씨는 신고를 받고 출동한 경찰관도 머리로 들이받았다. A씨는 1심에서 존속 폭행 및 공무집행방해 등 혐의로 징역 1년 6개월에 집행유예 4년을 선고받았다.

items.title: 출근길 시내버스 150m 폭주… 차량 32대 들이받고 70명 부상
items.snippet: 출근길 경기 성남에서 시내버스가 차량 32대를 연쇄 추돌하는 사고가 발생했다. 이 사고로 버스에 타고 있던 승객 등 70명이 다쳤다. 10명은 중상이다. 사고는 11일 오전 7시 34분쯤 분당구 판교로 벌말사거리 근처에서 발생했다. 60대 A씨가 몰던 340번 시내버스가 신호 대기 중이던 차량 등을 잇따라 들이받았다.

items.title: “전등·히터 끄는게 버릇” 티끌 모아 80억 기부
items.snippet: 지난 9일 찾은 경남 창원의 자동차 부품 업체 경한코리아 사옥 1층 로비는 한낮인데도 어두컴컴했다. 흐린 날씨에 로비 전등이 모두 꺼져 있었기 때문이다. 사옥 3층에 있는 이상연(77) 회장 집무실로 들어서자 냉기가 감돌았다. 히터를 틀지 않았다. 이 회장은 “전기료 아끼는 게 버릇이 됐다”고 했다. 경한코리아는 40년 넘게 형편이 어려운 아이들과 노인 등에게 80여억원을 기부했다.

items.title: 해외서 산 마운자로 국내 반입 가능
items.snippet: 12일부터 해외에서 정식 처방을 받아 구매한 비만 치료제 등 의약품을 최대 3개월분까지 국내에 갖고 들어올 수 있게 됐다. 식품의약품안전처(식약처)와 관세청은 12일부터 그동안 반입이 제한됐던 비만 치료제 등의 개인 휴대 반입을 허용한다고 11일 밝혔다. 그간 식약처는 유통·보관 과정을 확인하기 어렵고, 회수·보상 등 법적 보호에도 한계가 있다는 이유 등으로 개인이 해외에서 구매한 마운자로·위고비를 ‘유해 의약품’으로 분류해 반입을 제한해왔다. 관세청에 따르면 올해 1~8월 여행자 휴대품을 통한 마운자로·위고비 불법 반입 적발 건수는 1097건으로, 지난해 연간 134건의 약 8배였다. 해외 의료기관에서 정식 처방된 개인 치료용 의약품까지 반입을 막는 건 과도한 규제라는 지적도 제기됐다.

items.title: GTX-A 삼성역 이어 남산케이블카, 또다시 충돌하는 국토부와 서울시

items.title: 스텐트? 수술?… 관상동맥 핵심 부위 치료 30년 논쟁 종지부
items.snippet: 심장에 혈액을 공급하는 관상동맥에 협착이 있으면 심근경색이 발생하는데, 이 경우 흔히 스텐트 시술로 좁아진 관상동맥을 넓힌다. 전신마취를 하지 않고, 손목 동맥을 통해 가느다란 카테터를 관상동맥에 끼워서 금속 그물망 스텐트를 삽입해 넓힌다. 그런데 심장내과 의사들이 오랫동안 스텐트 넣는 것을 꺼렸던 곳이 있다. 심장의 왼쪽 관상동맥이 시작되는 좌주간부(Left Main Coronary Artery)다. 이곳은 심장 전체 혈류의 75% 이상을 공급하는, 두 개의 주요 관상동맥이 갈라져 나오는 관문이다. 고속도로에 비유하면 여러 주요 도로로 갈라지기 전의 핵심 진입로다. 좌주간부가 막히면 심장 근육 광범위한 영역이 혈액 공급을 잃어 생명이 위험해진다.

items.title: [Dr.이은봉의 의학 연구 다이제스트] 인공감미료 많이 먹으면 언어 유창성 급감
items.snippet: 설탕이 대사질환 발생 위험을 높인다고 알려지면서, 요즘 설탕 대신 단맛을 내는 인공감미료 섭취가 청량음료·스낵·디저트 음식 등을 통해 늘고 있다. 인공감미료로는 사카린, 아스파탐 등과 같은 합성 감미료와 에리스리톨, 소비톨 등과 같은 탄수화물 관련 감미료가 있다. 인공감미료는 칼로리가 거의 없기 때문에 대사질환 위험성이 낮을 것이라고 기대했지만, 당뇨, 심혈관질환, 암, 우울증 및 치매 발생과 관련성이 알려지고 있다. 이런 맥락 속에서 미국 신경학회지에 인공감미료가 인지기능에 얼마나 영향을 주는지 심층적으로 연구한 논문이 발표됐다.

items.title: 심장 쇼크 환자, 병원서 멀리 살수록 위험… 1시간 넘어 도착하면 사망률 38.8% 높아
items.snippet: 병원에서 멀리 떨어져 살수록 심장성 쇼크 환자의 사망률이 높다는 연구 결과가 나왔다. 병원 도착까지 60분 이상 걸리는 지역의 병원 내 사망률은 10분 미만 지역보다 약 1.5배 높았다. 심장성 쇼크는 심장 펌프 기능이 급격히 떨어져 온몸에 혈액이 제대로 돌지 않는 질환이다. 삼성서울병원 중환자의학과 양정훈, 순환기내과 최기홍, 임상역학연구센터 강단비 교수 공동 연구팀은 2017년부터 2022년까지 국내 상급종합병원 중환자실에 새로 입원한 성인 심장성 쇼크 환자 8만263명을 분석한 결과를 국제학술지 ‘중환자의학’ 최근 호에 발표했다.

items.snippet: 최근 메타가 내놓은 에이전트 앱 ‘뮤즈’를 소개한 적이 있었죠. 뮤즈의 두뇌로는 메타가 직접 만든 대규모 언어 모델(LLM) ‘뮤즈 스파크’가 쓰이는데, 챗GPT나 클로드에 견줄 만한 실력을 갖췄다는 평가를 받는다고 했죠. 그렇다면 메타는 언제부터 이렇게 LLM을 잘 만들게 됐을까요? 사실 메타가 LLM을 만든 역사는 결코 짧지 않습니다. 오픈AI가 챗GPT를 세상에 내놓은 게 2022년 11월인데, 석 달 뒤인 2023년 2월 메타도 LLM을 바로 내놓았거든요. 이름은 라마(LLaMA)예요. ‘메타 AI의 대규모 언어 모델(Large Language Model Meta AI)’을 줄인 말이죠. 그런데 메타는 오픈AI와 다른 길을 택했어요. 챗GPT처럼 이용자가 요구한 결과만 내놓는 식의 서비스를 제공할 뿐 아니라, LLM이 그 결과를 도출하...

items.snippet: 지금 남아있는 우리나라의 궁궐 건물 가운데 가장 오래된 것으로 알려진 서울 창덕궁 돈화문(敦化門)이 대대적인 보수 공사에 들어간다는 뉴스가 나왔어요. 국가유산청 궁능유적본부는 “국가유산 보물인 돈화문을 보수하기 위해 이번 달부터 지붕 해체에 착수한다”고 밝혔죠. 돈화문 보수 공사는 29년 만이랍니다. 2028년 10월 마무리될 예정이지만 해체와 조사 과정에서 수리 범위가 늘어나면 연장될 수 있다고 해요. 오늘은 이 돈화문이 어떤 문화유산인지 함께 살펴보겠습니다.

items.title: “좋은 일자리, 생애주기별 지원… 평균 연령 43.8세 郡 중 가장 젊은 도시”
items.snippet: 대구 달성군은 ‘젊은 도시’로 통한다. 지난해 기준 달성군 평균 연령은 43.8세로 전국 82개 군(郡) 중 가장 낮았다. 올해 9월 기준 달성군의 20~40대 인구 수는 전체 인구의 약 40%에 육박한다. 일자리와 보육 및 교육 환경 등이 갖춰지면서 대구 내 청년과 젊은 부부들이 입을 모아 ‘살기 좋은 곳’이라며 모여든 결과다.

items.title: Quantum Thermal Transistor via Nonlinear Environmental Coupling
items.abstract: Thermal amplification enables sensitive control of heat currents, providing a basis for heat management and thermal signal processing in quantum devices. For a harmonic oscillator coupled to emitter, collector, and base thermal reservoirs, we recover the absence of thermal amplification when system-reservoir interactions permit only single-quantum exchange. A controlled weak-nonlinearity expansion, supported by numerical stationary solutions, shows that two-quantum exchange at the emitter enables amplification and predicts its onset. When two-quantum exchange dominates at the emitter and collector, varying the base temperature redistributes populations between even and odd oscillator sectors. This changes the emitter and collector heat currents far more than the base current, enabling large thermal amplification. We propose a realization using a longitudinally coupled auxiliary two-level...

items.title: Analysis and Demonstration of a Current-Stiff, Isolated Capacitive Bridge Transformer
items.abstract: The traditional Voltage Source Inverter (VSI) based Dual Active Bridge (DAB) utilizes a transformer at its center to provide galvanic isolation and a turns ratio for step up/down functionality. However, the transformer is often the limiting factor of the DAB, especially as semiconductor switching speeds improve, given steel core losses, winding losses, etc. This paper presents a new DAB architecture based on Current Source Inverters (CSIs) coupled through, and isolated by, an AC capacitive bridge, yielding a system called a Capacitive Bridge Transformer (CBT). The CBT architecture eliminates all magnetic components in the AC portion of the isolated DAB circuit, reducing frequency scaling barriers normally present in DABs. items.abstract: Silicon carbide has emerged as a highly promising platform for scalable quantum technologies, with the silicon vacancy serving as a robust spin qubit and quantum sensor. However, conventional c-plane 4H-SiC restricts the experimental scheme and resonant optical excitation to the sample's geometry. The usage of a-plane substrates enables more versatile resonant optical access to the color center through the wafer surface. Here, we demonstrate the electrical control and optical addressability of $V_{2}$ (cubic lattice site) silicon vacancies within the intrinsic region of lateral pin-diodes fabricated on a-plane 4H-SiC wafers using a scalable complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) process. Despite extensive semiconductor processing, the integrated color centers exhibit good optical quality, evidenced by narrow optical transition linewidths below 80 MHz at zero bias. These embedded...

items.title: Nanostructuring Semiconductor Surfaces Using Self-Assembled Metal Nanoparticles for Optoelectronic Applications
items.abstract: Semiconductor nanostructures are key light-management elements because their geometry can strengthen light-matter interaction, suppress reflection, and enhance optical coupling. Yet their adoption across material platforms is constrained by lithography, multistep pattern transfer, persistent masks, and material-specific etching. Here, we introduce a lithography-free two-step strategy in which thermally evaporated self-assembled Ga nanoparticles act as self-consuming masks during Ar inductively coupled plasma reactive-ion etching. Correlated transmission electron microscopy on GaAs reveals the formation mechanism. Comparable erosion of the Ga nanoparticles and exposed substrate progressively converts Ga-capped pedestals into pure semiconductor nanocones while preserving crystalline order. items.title: From Growth to Devices: Oxygen-Controlled Superconductivity in BSCCO Thin Films
items.abstract: Realizing device-compatible high-$T_c$ superconductors requires simultaneous control of oxygen stoichiometry and tolerance to nanofabrication. Here, we investigate sputtered Bi$_2$Sr$_2$Ca$_{n-1}$Cu$_n$O$_{2n+4+δ}$ (BSCCO) thin films and establish a direct link between annealing conditions, oxygen incorporation, and superconducting transport. By independently varying the annealing temperature and duration, we identify an optimal annealing condition of $860\,^{\circ}$C for 3\,h, which yields the highest superconducting transition temperature and the narrowest transition among the investigated samples. X-ray diffraction, electron microscopy, and X-ray photoemission spectroscopy reveal a non-monotonic evolution of lattice oxygen, which governs hole doping in the CuO$_2$ planes and produces the characteristic dome-like dependence of $T_c$ on doping concentration. items.snippet: 30년 넘게 사업체를 운영해온 A씨는 2022년 한 공기업 납품 비리 사건과 관련해 공기업 간부와 납품업체 관계자 만남을 주선했다는 의혹을 받았다. 그보다 앞서 한 정치자금 위반 사건 재판에선 A씨가 모 정치인에게 금품을 전달했다는 진술이 나왔다. A씨는 두 사건과 관련해 범죄 혐의로 기소되지는 않았다. 미국에선 정관계 인맥을 이용해 행정부나 의회를 상대로 활동하는 사람을 ‘로비스트’라 부른다. 미국에선 로비스트가 합법이다. 그러나 한국에선 A씨처럼 정치인·공직자와 업자를 연결하거나 정치인을 음성적으로 후원하는 사람을 ‘브로커’라 부른다. 합법과 불법 경계를 오간다는 부정적 이미지가 강한 개념이다.

items.title: SLIC: Reinforcement Fine-Tuning Small LMs for Multi-Turn Analog Circuit Optimization
items.abstract: Analog integrated circuit (IC) design is a multi-turn, simulator-grounded engineering task that demands iterative reasoning over coupled performance tradeoffs, yet proprietary process design kits (PDKs) make hosted large language model workflows difficult to deploy in practical design settings. We present SLIC (Small LM Iterating on Circuits), a reinforcement fine-tuning framework that trains a 4B-scale, locally deployable language model for closed-loop analog circuit optimization. SLIC pairs structured circuit representations with discretized relative-update actions, domain- and success-gated multiobjective rewards, and Reward-Guided Rollout Steering (RGRS), which turns per-step simulator feedback into signals for both policy learning and online rollout construction in this sparse, highly constrained domain. items.title: 5G CATS: 5G-Based Cryptographic Authorization Against Trafficking of Semiconductor Devices
items.abstract: Enforcing export controls on AI accelerators requires verifying where a chip operates after deployment. Round-trip time measurements can bound a chip's distance from a trusted landmark, but any jitter in honest replies forces the verifier to loosen its timeout, giving an attacker slack to relay traffic over fiber from a restricted region. Prior approaches either cross the untrusted host stack or rely on noisy power-line channels that inflate this slack. We present 5G CATS, a location certification system that pairs a co-packaged 5G radio, cryptographic engine, and hardware interlock on the GPU package with 5G Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communication (URLLC) base stations. Terminating the radio link inside the package removes the host software, PCIe fabric, and baseboard management controller from the verification path. items.title: Ultrafast Hole Transport and Electron Localization in Superatomic Re$_{6}$Se$_{8}$Cl$_{2}$
items.abstract: Van der Waals superatomic crystals represent an intriguing class of materials, exhibiting unique ultrafast electronic and structural responses arising from their hierarchical crystal structure. These materials bridge the properties of semiconductors, molecular solids, and nanocrystal arrays, hosting a range of many-body interactions that can be controlled with atomically precise structures. To establish the structure-function correlation, it is necessary to understand element-specific electronic states arising from complex superatomic unit cells. Here, we use transient XUV spectroscopy to individually probe the dynamics of photoexcited electrons and holes in Re$_{6}$Se$_{8}$Cl$_{2}$ superatomic crystals. items.abstract: Physical synapses are routinely described by a single number, the weight, that is identified with a conductance, a current, or a luminescence yield. This identification conflates two different objects: the internal state that the device stores, and the signal obtained when that state is read. items.abstract: We study the spin-1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnet with an anisotropic $Γ$ term on a zigzag ladder, which can be exactly mapped to the spin-1/2 XYZ zigzag ladder by a spin rotation. This model has recently attracted considerable interest as an effective model for the quasi-one-dimensional magnetic semiconductor YbCuS$_2$. For the model, the ground-state phase diagram was previously proposed by Saito and Hotta [Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 166701 (2024); Phys. Rev. B 110, 024409 (2024)]. We systematically reexamine the phase diagram through complementary numerical and analytical approaches, including exact diagonalization, the density-matrix renormalization group method, and low-energy effective theories. items.title: Spin-valve effect through electrostatic coupling
items.abstract: We propose a spin-valve effect in which an insulating magnetic van der Waals multilayer controls the conductance of an adjacent non-magnetic conductor by electrostatic coupling, without transport-electrons entering the magnetic layers. We consider two types of coupling and device concepts: charge transfer to a graphene monolayer and capacitive coupling in a single-electron transistor. We use density functional calculations to assess the magnitude of the effect in various materials, including CrI$_3$, CrBr$_3$, CrCl$_3$ and NiBr$_2$. items.title: Gate-tunable supercurrent switching in a three-terminal quantum dot transistor
items.abstract: We propose and analyze a three-terminal superconducting transistor switch in which a gate-defined quantum dot region interrupts a flux-controlled loop. The output supercurrent is switched off completely when the two loop arms couple to the dot with equal tunneling strengths and half a flux quantum threads the loop. The device then operates as a symmetric SQUID at half flux. The condition follows from a single geometric factor $χ$, which reduces the three-terminal problem to an equivalent two-terminal Anderson impurity model and makes the switching mechanism independent of the Coulomb interaction, the dot level position, the total hybridization and temperature. These enter only through a prefactor and thus decide how tolerant the device is to imperfect barrier tuning. items.abstract: The layered van der Waals semiconductor CrSBr combines intrinsic magnetic order with semiconducting and optical properties, making it a promising material for multifunctional electronic and photonic applications. Understanding how defects and structural transformations affect its properties under experimentally relevant conditions, however, remains challenging for first-principles simulations due to the relevant length and time scales. Here, we develop and benchmark machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) for the Cr-S-Br system, enabling large-scale atomistic simulations of CrSBr with accuracy approaching that of density functional theory (DFT). The charge-aware variant qNEP achieves near-DFT accuracy in predicting lattice constants, formation enthalpies, vacancy energetics, and the anisotropic pressure response of o-CrSBr. items.title: Impact of multi-dot configurations on electron temperature and double quantum dot latching in gate-controlled qubit devices
items.abstract: Many currently envisaged scalable architectures for Si/SiGe spin qubit devices utilize gate-controlled multi-dot configurations characterized by their peculiar Coulomb blockade physics. One example is the concurrent use of a single electron transistor (SET) as a charge sensor and as a reservoir for adjacent qubit quantum dots (QD). We find that the SET energy spectrum impacts pulsed gate spectroscopy of the QD when the SET simultaneously acts as the reservoir and the sensor. Then, using the qubit QD as a probe, we quantify how strongly the electron temperature of the SET depends on the applied bias. It surpasses a reference experiment by 100 $mK$ even at 50 $μV$ bias. Our results provide a strong incentive for choosing spin qubit initialization schemes which do not rely on coupling to the reservoir in such devices. items.title: Environmental Assessment of GaN Current-Source and Voltage-Source AC-AC Variable Speed Drives
items.abstract: Three-phase ac-ac converters for variable-speed drives can be realized conventionally as voltage-source converters (VSCs) or, leveraging emerging monolithic bidirectional GaN power transistors (M-BDSs), as current-source converters (CSCs). This paper presents a comparative life-cycle assessment of a realized VSC and a CSC demonstrators including grid-side and motor-side EMI filters, and with identical specifications (1.4 kW rated power, 200 V line-to-line rms grid and motor voltage). The embodied carbon footprints are similar (44.8 kgCO2eq for the VSC and 47.4 kgCO2eq for the CSC) and dominated by auxiliary and control electronics, and the printed circuit boards. items.title: Rapid Heat Removal from Chip Cores: Near-Junction Active Cooling of Power Transistors via Electron Entropy Transport and Spatial Decoupling
items.abstract: Chip performance is limited by a shared bottleneck: the core produces heat faster than it can be moved out. We study the hardest case, RF power GaN HEMTs, whose hotspots exceed 5 kW/cm^2, and propose a horizontal near-junction active cooling topology built on electron entropy transport. Classical on-chip thermoelectric cooling faces a contest: Peltier absorption grows linearly with current, Joule heating with its square. In a vertical pillar, its own conduction resistance locks about half the Joule heat back toward the cold end, capping net cooling. From the Onsager framework we show the origin of this asymmetry: Peltier absorption localizes at the interface where the Seebeck coefficient jumps, whereas Joule heating fills the volume. items.title: Orbital texture of valence band and interband transitions of the type-II multiferroic van der Waals NiI$_2$
items.abstract: NiI$_2$ is a van der Waals semiconductor characterized by complex electronic and magnetic phases, holding promise towards functional applications. For this purpose, a detailed understanding of its band structure and its excitations is essential to elucidate the electronic and transport properties. We present a comprehensive description of the band structure and of the lowest valence-to-conduction band transition in bulk NiI$_2$, by means of time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy supported by first-principles calculations. We describe the orbital character of Ni and I manifolds, and identify the main momentum-resolved features of the valence band and the shallow minima of the conduction band. With this study, we provide a foundational understanding of the electronic structure of NiI$_2$ and its single-particle interband electronic excitation, a benchmark for theoretical model...

items.title: A Per-Step Load-Balancing Engine for Expert-Parallel MoE Serving
items.abstract: In expert-parallel Mixture-of-Experts serving, a layer finishes only when the most loaded GPU of its group does. Token routing shifts at every decode step and concentrates on a few experts, so most of the group's reserved GPU time waits on stragglers. Recovering that time means re-deciding, at every layer of every decode step, how each replicated expert's tokens divide between its copies. The exact linear-program solvers that make this decision optimally take longer than many of the layers they serve, and their working set outgrows GPU shared memory at deployment scale. We introduce Relief, a bidirectional pairwise relaxation that makes the linear program unnecessary, coming within a fraction of a point of the per-step optimum in a few passes of integer halving over the token counts. items.title: ICLayout-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Custom Circuit Layout Design
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are being explored for circuit design, but their ability to produce high-quality custom layouts has not been extensively evaluated. ICLayout-Bench is a benchmark in which agents use electronic design automation (EDA) tools to construct and optimize GDSII layouts from transistor-level circuit netlists. These layouts are evaluated using physical verification, parasitic extraction, and post-layout simulation. Layouts that pass the physical and functional checks are scored on electrical performance and area. The benchmark includes 165 tasks across 13 process design kits (PDKs), covering technology nodes from 3 nm to 180 nm. The tasks span analog, mixed-signal, and digital circuits in open-source and commercial EDA flows. The experiments evaluate 22 configurations spanning seven models on 21 public and 19 private tasks. items.title: $>3\text{ W/mm}$ Output Power $\mathrm{Al}_{0.61}\mathrm{Ga}_{0.39}\mathrm{N}$ Channel HEMT with $24.4\%$ Associated PAE at $10\text{ GHz}$
items.abstract: In this work, an ultra-wide bandgap (UWBG) high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) was fabricated using an $\mathrm{Al}_{0.76}\mathrm{Ga}_{0.24}\mathrm{N}$ barrier and an $\mathrm{Al}_{0.61}\mathrm{Ga}_{0.39}\mathrm{N}$ channel with thick $\mathrm{SiO}_2$ passivation. The device demonstrated low current collapse at $40\text{ V}$ drain bias. At $10\text{ GHz}$, the device exhibited an output power of $3.07\text{ W/mm}$ with an associated power-added efficiency (PAE) of $24.4\%$. A peak PAE of $33.9\%$ was achieved at an associated output power of $2.14\text{ W/mm}$. This excellent large-signal performance highlights the strong potential of UWBG $\mathrm{AlGaN}$ channel devices for X-band applications.

The devices featured a recessed T-gate structure and $\mathrm{SiO_2}$ passivation. Devices with larger dimensions demonstrated a high off-state breakdown voltage of 883 V and an $f_{\mathrm{T}}$ of 24 GHz, yielding a high Johnson's figure of merit ($\mathrm{JFOM}$) of 21.19 $\mathrm{THz \cdot V}$. items.title: Deterministically fabricated C-band single-photon sources based on quantum dot circular Bragg grating cavities
items.abstract: Telecom-wavelength quantum light sources are essential components for scalable fiber-based quantum networks, where on-demand emission of single photons is required for high secret key rates. Here, we demonstrate the deterministic integration of metal-organic vapor-phase epitaxy (MOVPE)-grown C-band InAs/InP quantum dots into circular Bragg grating resonators. The integrated emitters exhibit a radiative lifetime of $T_1 = (1400 \pm 50)~\mathrm{ps}$ and a spectral linewidth of $ΔE_{\mathrm{FWHM}} = (41.0 \pm 4.0)~μ\mathrm{eV}$. Under non-resonant excitation, we measure a post-selected single-photon purity of $(0.95 \pm 0.02)$ and a raw two-photon interference visibility of $V_{12\mathrm{ns}} = (35 \pm 2)\%$, which increases to $(70 \pm 18)\%$ under temporal post-selection. items.abstract: Ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) with low-power operation and non-volatile data retention enabled by stable ferroelectric polarization switching, have emerged as promising alternatives to conventional floating-gate transistors for next-generation low-power memory applications. In this work, we report wafer scale 2D semiconductor-based FeFETs with Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 (HZO) gate stack showing unusual p-type charge transport and stable multibit memory properties. items.title: Fabrication and Characterization of Flexible In2O3 Thin-Film Transistors on Mica Substrates
items.abstract: Flexible oxide-semiconductor thin-film transistors (TFTs) with high field-effect mobility (uFE > 70 cm^2/Vs) are required for next-generation flexible displays. Polycrystalline In2O3-based TFTs are promising candidates; however, conventional flexible substrates such as plastics are not suitable because their fabrication typically requires relatively high temperatures (~350 deg.C). In this study, we used mica as a flexible substrate to fabricate polycrystalline In2O3-based TFTs, motivated by previous demonstrations of crystalline oxide growth on mica. The resulting TFTs exhibited a uFE of approximately 75 cm^2/Vs. The devices maintained gate-modulated operation after 10^3 flex-out bending cycles at a 5 mm radius, whereas flex-in cycling caused early electrical failure, likely due to In2O3 film degradation. items.title: The World Model Planning Accelerator (WMPA): Hardware-Algorithm Co-Design for Embedded AI in Robotics
items.abstract: Embedded AI is moving from perception to prediction. Robots now use world models$\unicode{x2014}$learned simulators that predict the outcome of candidate actions in a compressed latent space before any is executed. Every predicted step must be computed on board within a tight power and thermal budget, yet the energy these steps fundamentally require, and how far real hardware sits from it, have not been characterized. We derive lower bounds on the arithmetic operations and the CMOS dynamic energy of a latent state transition from information theory and Boolean circuit complexity. Profiling a DreamerV3-style Recurrent State Space Model (RSSM) shows that every rollout operation is memory-bandwidth bound and that a GPU consumes at least $5.9\times10^{10}$ times the CMOS energy floor. items.title: How light interacts with matter, revisited
items.abstract: In 1968 Victor Weisskopf explained in Scientific American how light interacts with matter, with a few formulas and many words. We tell the same story again with the tools that have since become available: the fields are computed and drawn, and their evolution in time is shown in animations. Light is described as a classical electromagnetic field and matter as a collection of charged oscillators; every phenomenon follows from adding up the retarded waves radiated by the oscillators, each with its proper delay and phase. items.title: Controlled Oxidation of Tellurium Nanoparticles for Telecom Detection
items.abstract: Surface oxidation plays an important role in governing charge transport in semiconductor nanoparticle assemblies. Here, we investigate the optoelectronic properties of solution-processed tellurium (Te) nanoparticle ensembles prepared through gradual ambient-air exposure. Structural and spectroscopic analyses reveal interconnected elemental Te nanoparticles with coexisting alpha-TeO2 and hydroxyl-containing surface species, exhibiting a lower relative contribution of oxidized Te than previously investigated forced-air-oxidized ensembles. The resulting photodetectors demonstrate photoresponse at 405, 532, and 1550 nm, with maximum responsivities of 10.1, 14.4, and 8.5 mA/W, respectively. items.title: Trajectory-Dependent Decoherence and Leakage During Shuttling of Multi-Spin Qubits
items.abstract: Logical qubits encoded in collective states of multiple spins are promising building blocks for large-scale semiconductor quantum processors. As novel fault-tolerant architectures increasingly rely on qubit shuttling, understanding decoherence of the shuttled multi-spin qubits becomes crucial. We analyze fidelity and leakage of the logical qubits dephased by the spatio-temporally correlated $1/f$ noise, considering two-, three-, and four-spin encodings. We study different shuttling protocols and establish that for all encodings generally, parallel shuttling provides the best protection against decoherence at short distances, whereas sequential shuttling outperforms others for long-range transport (although the exact boundaries depend on the specific device parameters). items.title: Discrete time crystals and heteroclinic switching in actively mode-locked semiconductor lasers
items.abstract: We investigate the mechanisms underlying the emergence of discrete time crystals in actively mode-locked semiconductor lasers. Our analysis is based on a Haus master equation generalized to retain carrier memory between round-trips. We perform a detailed bifurcation analysis that reveals a well-defined hierarchy of subharmonic states, illustrating how pulses may suppress their neighbors when the modulation runs faster than the pulse round-trip frequency. To identify the underlying mechanism, we derive effective equations of motion that couple the pulse energies, their positions relative to the modulation transmission maxima, and the local time-dependent gain. These reveal that transitions between time-crystalline states occur via transcritical global bifurcations, opening a regime of heteroclinic winnerless competition between symmetry-degenerate configurations.

items.title: Microscopic theory of exciton polarons in transition metal dichalcogenides
items.abstract: Polarons are composite quasiparticles formed when charge carriers strongly couple to lattice vibrations, manifesting as carriers dressed by a surrounding cloud of phonons. Although this dressing fundamentally renormalizes the effective mass and mobility of carriers, its impact on electrically neutral exciton polarons in 2D semiconductors has received limited attention. In particular, despite the growing interest in polaronic effects in atomically thin semiconductors, only a few theoretical studies have addressed spectral signatures and renormalized properties of exciton polarons in these materials. Here, we develop a microscopic model to describe exciton polarons in transition metal dichalcogenides. items.title: Exciton design via topological spin textures
items.abstract: Excitons carry energy and information through a semiconductor without carrying charge. This makes them attractive for optoelectronics, but also hard to guide. Magnetic skyrmions, on the other hand, are moved by small electrical currents. Here we develop a theory of excitons interacting with a skyrmion in which the electron and the hole are treated as distinct constituents, each with its own spin--orbit coupling. We find that the topology of the skyrmion is transferred to the exciton only when the exchange coupling exceeds the relevant spin--orbit splitting. The exciton then experiences a full flux quantum, with opposite signs in the two valleys. The quantum metric of the spin texture creates a ring-shaped barrier that traps excitons, whereas the topological charge fixes the angular momentum of the trapped states and hence their optical selection rules. items.title: On the collective flow puzzle in ultra-central heavy-ion collisions
items.abstract: Using UCC-DiffHIC, an AI-accelerated event-by-event hydrodynamic model validated against hybrid simula- tions, we study flow in ultracentral Pb-Pb collisions. For suitable initial conditions, the calculated v2{2}/v3{2} approaches unity in the most central collisions, consistent with experiment. An exact response decomposition shows that residual fluctuations suppress the ratio through P3/P2 < 1, where P2 and P3 are Pearson response correlations for elliptic and triangular flow, respectively. This resolves the apparent flow hierarchy without requiring a breakdown of linear response or additional effects such as nuclear deformation.

items.abstract: Conventional thermal emitters obey Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation, which requires emissivity and absorptivity to be equal at each wavelength, angle, and polarization. This in turn places a fundamental limit on a range of radiative energy technologies as well as heat transfer. This constraint can however be overcome using magneto-optic semiconductors, which break Lorentz reciprocity under an applied magnetic field. However, in most prior experimental demonstrations, nonreciprocity has been restricted to TM polarization, since the electric field of TE-polarized light is parallel to the applied magnetic field. items.title: Asymptotic-Preserving Tensor Neural Networks for 3D High-Field Kinetic Equations with Applications to Uncertainty Quantification
items.abstract: Kinetic equations in the high-field regime describe particle transport dominated by electric-field acceleration and collisional relaxation. These equations are widely used in simulations of plasmas and semiconductor devices. Typical models include the Vlasov--Poisson--Fokker--Planck (VPFP) and Boltzmann--Poisson systems. Their high dimensionality and multiscale nature pose two of the major challenges to accurate and efficient numerical solution. To address these challenges, we propose an asymptotic-preserving tensor neural network (APTNN) method. Specifically, to reduce high-dimensional computational costs and memory requirements, we adopt the canonical polyadic (CP) decomposition structure of TNNs to approximate their solutions. The $Ξ$ and $V$ manifolds are selected from the exciton spectrum by systematically screening optical brightness, intra-excitonic dipole strength and state compactness, making the selection reproducible and transferable to other materials. items.title: Micius-Flash: Lightweight Agentic Intelligence for Engineering
items.abstract: We introduce Micius-Flash, a 27-billion-parameter model for engineering with native multimodal input, deep reasoning and a 256K-token context window. We design the Micius data pipeline as a knowledge-tree-driven data flywheel comprising three stages: knowledge tree construction and expansion, data synthesis, and quality validation with hard-example augmentation. From this data, we train expert models for semiconductor knowledge and reasoning, hardware coding, and semiconductor multimodal understanding, along with agentic experts. Subsequently, we employ Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD) to supervise training on sequences generated by Micius itself, thereby integrating the capabilities of these expert models into a unified model. items.abstract: Parametric amplifiers are a workhorse for near-quantum-limited measurements above 1 GHz. However, amplifier development has been more limited below 1 GHz. The system noise performance, as measured by a variable-temperature noise source, is 2.5-3.5 quanta. This device is a versatile new tool for precision measurements of sub-GHz signals, with applications including readout of semiconductor spin qubits, superconducting detector arrays, and searches for new physics beyond the Standard Model. items.abstract: Every reconfigurable microwave device places a tuning element - a varactor, a diode, transistor, microelectromechanical or phase-change switch, a ferroelectric or liquid-crystal load - inside a fixed passive network. items.abstract: Electrostatic control is central to the operation of semiconductor junctions made from conventional materials. Here, we theoretically investigate the electrostatic properties of lateral junctions between two-dimensional (2D) Chern semiconductors in a perpendicular magnetic field. As a consequence, two regions with different Chern numbers acquire different chemical potentials at charge neutrality, leading to a built-in potential of topological origin across the junction. items.abstract: Bonding semiconductors to substrates with high thermal conductivity is a promising way to solve the heat-dissipation problem of materials that transport heat poorly, and it avoids the lattice-matching constraints of conventional epitaxy. However, the lattice mismatch remains, leaving the two materials with mismatched phonon states, while poor interface quality scatters phonons even more. Together, these effects block phonon transport across the bonded interface and make interfacial thermal resistance a critical bottleneck, calling for careful interface engineering. Here, $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC serves as a model system for a phonon-bridging strategy. items.title: Time-resolved infrared spectroscopy with entangled photons and visible-light detection
items.abstract: Time-resolved infrared (TR-IR) spectroscopy reveals molecular structural changes and charge-carrier dynamics on their intrinsic timescales, in photosynthesis, catalysis and optoelectronic materials, but requires complex sources of ultrashort infrared pulses, cryogenically cooled detectors to overcome thermal background, and intense probes that can perturb the sample. Quantum infrared spectroscopy avoids these constraints: harnessing quantum interference between the generation processes of frequency-entangled photon pairs, it reads out the infrared response of a sample by detecting only the visible partner photon, for which efficient detectors exist. To date, it has been limited to steady-state measurements. Here we demonstrate its ultrafast, time-resolved form with a picosecond visible pump pulse and a silicon detector. items.abstract: Extreme events often occur sequentially, from earthquake-tsunami cascades to successive extreme losses in financial markets. We introduce an extremal token representation that encodes multivariate observations as a categorical sequence. items.title: Optical Ceiling on Polaron Mobility in Disordered Molecular Semiconductors: Lessons from Eumelanin
items.abstract: Polaron hopping in disordered molecular semiconductors such as eumelanin is set by energetic disorder $σ$ and reorganization energy $λ$. We show that the reduced polaron absorption band encodes this transport problem. Its value at zero energy fixes the mean hop rate, which bounds the mobility in any dimension. For Gaussian disorder and classical vibrations its centroid is $E_\mathrm{op}=λ+(1-c)σ^2/k_BT$, its variance obeys the Hush relation, and the bound is the Marcus rate at $λ\to E_\mathrm{op}$; a 1D lower bound vanishes at $k_BT^*=(1-c)σ^2/λ$, read from optics.

items.title: Generalized Lorentz Framework for Active Semiconductor Quantum Surface Plasmonics
items.abstract: Nanostructured semiconductors provide an actively tunable platform for light-matter interactions across a broad spectral range. As feature sizes shrink to the deep nanoscale (~10 nm scale), nonclassical carrier dynamics and surface plasmonic responses become prominent, creating substantial challenges for a rigorous and efficient theoretical treatment. Here we develop a generalized Lorentz framework for quantum surface plasmonics in nanostructured semiconductors with arbitrary energymomentum dispersion relations. The framework enables efficient quantitative treatment of carrier nonlocality, carrier surface accumulation and depletion, and nonlocal damping in three-dimensional semiconductor nanostructures, under electrical tuning and across a wide range of doping densities. Building on this framework, we further establish a rigorous quasinormal-mode analysis that provides transparent physic...

items.title: A RISC-V Simulator for the Tenstorrent Tensix Architecture
items.abstract: RISC-V based AI accelerators have become popular and not only for AI and ML, but also as vehicles for exploring HPC workloads more generally. Tenstorrent are one example, and whilst they document their Tensix architecture in detail and develop their software stack openly, running code has historically required a physical card, and their recently released simulator targets hardware equivalence rather than introspection. In this paper we present Wolfpine, a community developed RISC-V simulator for the Tensix architecture, supporting both the Wormhole and Blackhole generations and integrating seamlessly with the TT-Metal software stack. Constructed entirely from publicly available documentation, open source software and measurements on physical hardware, Wolfpine is written in pure Python for readability and ease of modification. An opt-in, provenance-tracked cost model adds timing fidelity...

items.title: Effect of compensation on magnetic ordering in (Ga,Mn)As
items.abstract: The real mechanism of ferromagnetism in III-V diluted magnetic semiconductors such as Ga$_{1-x}$Mn$_x$As is still debated. The experimental results point out the realization of appreciable ferromagnetism at filling of the impurity band close to one-half that can be expressed in terms of compensation degree. Based on our recent results on the existence of two competing mechanisms of pair indirect exchange (with ferro- and antiferro alignment of Mn $d$ shells), a theory of magnetic ordering in (Ga,Mn)As is presented. The molecular-field-like equation is derived in which the effective exchange constant contains all necessary information about material, including the Mn content, the compensation degree, the crystal coordination, and the parameters of two competing pair exchange interactions. The Curie temperature depends crucially on the compensation degree. Depending on Mn content and compe...

A simple bilayer square lattice with a two-atom unit cell, not limited to small lattice spacings, provides near-unity reflectionless transmission and a full $2π$ phase control of transmitted light without the localized site-dependent level shifts of previous proposals. This simplification is achieved through nonlocal radiative excitations that provide the familiar electric-dipole response with even radiation parity as well as an odd-parity radiation channel whose leading multipolar interpretation combines magnetic-dipole and electric-quadrupol...

items.title: Analytically Calibrated Upper L-Statistics for High-Dimensional Mean Change-Point Testing
items.abstract: This paper develops upper L-statistic methods for testing and localizing a high-dimensional mean change. At each candidate split, the proposed statistics rank the squared studentized CUSUM values across coordinates and aggregate either a fixed number or a fixed proportion of the largest entries. This construction connects max-type and sum-type procedures and provides sensitivity to a wide range of sparsity regimes. We establish asymptotic null distributions under an independent-component representation allowing weak cross-sectional dependence. The limiting laws are Poisson tangent processes for fixed ranks and Gaussian-process or Gumbel laws for proportional ranks. To improve finite-sample performance, we develop analytic calibrations for marginal variance estimation, cross-sectional dependence, extreme clustering, and skewness, and establish their first-order validity. We combine calibr...

However, direct high-throughput measurement of individual chip warpage remains difficult in mass-production environments, while existing wafer-level metrology systems routinely provide dense 3D shape data at the wafer scale. This paper proposes a Bezier-surface-based Gaussian Process---known as Bezier-GP---for chips-on-wafer warpage modeling. items.abstract: With the development of cryogenic technologies such as quantum computing, there is an increasing need for low-power cryogenic thermometers that minimize self-heating. Here, we report an anomalous temperature-independent logarithmic current slope, $d(\ln J)/dV$, in heavily doped silicon p$^{+}$n$^{+}$ junctions with significant dopant interdiffusion and highlight the advantages of our device as a low-power, cryogenic thermometer. Electrical characterizations from 2 to 420 K reveal that, at low forward bias, $d(\ln J)/dV$ remains nearly constant, which yields a voltage-temperature responsivity that is nearly independent of bias current. The observed transport cannot be fully understood with conventional diffusion or direct band-to-band tunneling. Instead, the results suggest the contribution of trap-assisted tunneling. items.title: Polariton tweezers
items.abstract: The non-invasive, deterministic manipulation of charge carriers remains a fundamental challenge in solid-state quantum technologies. Here, we demonstrate the concept of dynamic polariton tweezers capable of trapping and transporting electrons across a two-dimensional electron system via the long-range electrostatic potential of dipolar (d-) exciton-polaritons. By driving a semiconductor microcavity with a specifically engineered, non-collinear three-beam optical pump with TE-polarization, we synthesize a macroscopic polariton lattice with hexagonal symmetry. The spatially periodic field of this d-polariton condensate acts as a reconfigurable trapping landscape for the electrons. items.title: Cage-enforced i-wave altermagnetism in boron-carbon clathrates
items.abstract: The spin splitting of an altermagnet arises from a rotation that relates its two magnetic sublattices. In known cases it is fixed by the crystal structure. Here we show that guest-host frameworks separate the two roles. In the boron-carbon clathrates $M$B$_3$C$_3$ the ordered cage removes the translation between the two guest sites and enforces cubic $i$-wave altermagnetism, with six symmetry-enforced nodal planes, for any magnetic guest in the compensated state; strain retunes the class to $d$- or $g$-wave. We demonstrate the platform with GdB$_3$C$_3$: its compensated antiferromagnetic ground state is a narrow-gap semiconductor with spin splitting of 0.19 eV at the conduction-band edge, and its weakly pinned Néel vector switches the helicity-resolved optical response on and off according to the magnetic point group. items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate the kinetics of attachment of new segments of the crystalline lattice (pyramids) at steps on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs(-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb(-1-1-1) surfaces. Diffusion species are gallium adatoms at high coverage or gallium adatoms connected with nonmetal atom creating stable pyramids. These pyramids arrive at the steps, and cannot be attached be directly because the Ga adatom at the pyramid base cannot be attached directly. Therefore they are incorporated into the step by additional nonmetal atoms glue atoms arriving from the vapor or detached from other segments of the surface terraces.

The pyramidal structures are stable during surface jumps involving rotations around one of the basal Ga adatoms. Thus, the diffusion proceeds via rotation (pivot) of the pair of the other basal Ga adatoms around an immobile Ga adatom moving them into new, originally empty sites. We investigate cross-domain self-supervised pretraining using joint-embedding predictive architecture for heterogeneous industrial time series (JEPA-HITS), which learns one encoder from various domains such as battery, semiconductor chemical mechanical planarization (CMP), computer numerical control (CNC) machining, and bearing while preserving dataset-specific temporal scales. We evaluate representation reuse on regression and classification problems under reduced-label downstream training, and leave-one-domain-out (LODO) pretraining. Compared with the same architecture initialized randomly, LODO pretraining reduces RMSE from 10.72 to 7.95 on battery remaining useful life (RUL), 4.34 to 3.89 on CMP, and 13.53 to 11.72 on tool wear regression, while im...

items.title: Gate-tunable superconductor-semiconductor coupling and its impact on zero-energy modes in PbTe-Pb nanowires
items.abstract: Superconductor-semiconductor coupling in hybrid nanowires plays a pivotal role in Majorana devices. Here, we demonstrate this tunable coupling in PbTe-Pb nanowires and its impact on the induced gap and zero-bias peaks (ZBPs). In the strong coupling regime, the device reveals a clean superconducting gap, where robust and non-robust ZBPs are observed in distinct magnetic field ranges. Conversely, increasing the gate voltage drives the system toward the weak coupling regime, where the gap becomes narrow and soft. Consequently, robust ZBPs disappear while non-robust ones persist. Our results establish a direct link between tunable coupling and robust ZBPs, providing guidelines on engineering Majorana zero modes and topological qubits.

items.title: Amplification of valley polarization in an hBN-separated MoSe2-WSe2 heterostructure
items.abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenide heterostructures host long-lived interlayer excitons in the +K and -K valleys that can encode long-lived valley polarization. We investigated the low-temperature valley polarization dynamics in an MoSe2-bilayer hBN-WSe2 heterostructure. The bilayer hBN spacer results in an interlayer exciton lifetime exceeding 2 μs and an anomalous valley polarization amplification effect. Our theoretical model shows that this amplification results from the long exciton lifetime and exciton-exciton interactions. This work sets the stage for long-lived interlayer excitons to be used in nonlinear valleytronic transistors and amplifiers.

The primary limitation is that traditional methods depend on precise thickness measurements or are restricted to crystalline materials. In this work, we present an in-situ, non-destructive optical methodology to determine the CTE of suspended nanofilms by tracking the temperature-dependence of their vibrational frequency. This approach eliminates thickness measurements entirely and works for amorphous films where X-ray diffraction (XRD) fails. We experimentally validate this technique across a broad temperature range, evaluating membranes in their native microstructure state without requiring additional destructive patterning or complex sam...

items.title: Band Alignment of Grafted versus Directly Bonded Si/Ge Heterostructures

items.title: Coherent Optical Control of a Single Donor Electron Spin
items.abstract: Coherent spin--photon interfaces for scalable quantum networks require bright optical transitions, long-lived spin coherence, and complete coherent spin control. Donor spins in direct-bandgap semiconductors combine strong donor-bound exciton transitions with a potentially nuclear-spin-free environment. However, coherent control of an individual optically active donor spin has remained elusive. Here, we demonstrate coherent optical control of a single Cl donor electron spin in ZnSe. Resonant excitation reveals spin relaxation dynamics and measures spin coherence through coherent population trapping (CPT). Off-resonant ultrafast pulses are implemented to drive spin Rabi oscillations and demonstrate Ramsey interference. Multiple dark resonances in the CPT spectrum further reveal hyperfine coupling between the electron and the I=3/2 Cl nucleus. Together, these results demonstrate the first c...

items.title: Online Open-World Wafer Defect Discovery using Hyperdimensional Computing
items.abstract: Conventional wafer defect analysis relies on offline, closed-world classifiers that fail to detect novel, unseen defect signatures emerging during continuous semiconductor manufacturing. To address this, we propose WaferHDC, an online open-world wafer defect discovery framework based on hyperdimensional computing (HDC). The memory-centric architecture of WaferHDC enables rapid anomaly detection and grouping of recurring failures into compact hypervector representations. This allows the memory space to dynamically scale with new defect modes without retraining a static classifier or archiving entire raw wafer history. WaferHDC first models normal spatial distributions, then dynamically groups recurring failures into persistent defect memory without labels or predefined class counts. items.abstract: We describe the nanofabrication and loading of lithographically patterned, high aspect ratio $10$ $μ$m diameter silicon dioxide discs with thickness of $400$ nm into an optical standing wave trap in vacuum. We obtain motional spectra of the center of mass motion of the discs using a combination of interferometric and imaging methods. The method is capable of high-efficiency loading and optical trapping using small numbers of objects, of the order of a few particles, with customized geometries and sizes compatible with wafer scale nanofabrication methods. Disc-like particles in optical traps have been identified as promising candidates for detectors of high frequency gravitational waves or as sensitive accelerometers.

items.title: Residual AM and PM Noise of Selected X-Band Amplifiers
items.abstract: In microwave systems design, amplitude modulation (AM) noise is often ignored relative to phase modulation (PM) noise. However, in high-performance applications requiring ultra-low PM noise, AM noise becomes a critical limiting factor due to AM-to-PM conversion mechanisms. Because AM noise specifications are rarely, if ever, provided for commercial microwave components, this study characterizes the residual AM and PM noise of several 10 GHz amplifiers. We present performance data for various Heterojunction Bipolar Transistor (HBT) amplifier designs and demonstrate the noise reduction achieved through power-summed configurations. For example, a discrete-die GaAs HBT amplifier achieves residual PM noise below $-160$ dBrad$^2$/Hz and AM noise of approximately $-155$ dB/Hz at a 1 kHz offset in a quad power-summed configuration. A notable finding is that the majority of amplifier designs surv...

items.title: Hierarchical Fourier Phase Projection for Local Electronic Observables
items.abstract: In this letter, we develop hierarchical Fourier phase projection (HPP) for the calculation of local electronic observables. The method couples the spatial decay of the density matrix with a hierarchy of Fourier probes, improving accuracy through refinement, and making use of all previously evaluated responses. The variation in the calculated observables during the refinement process carries information on the residual error. We use a locality-based model to estimate the error from these changes with no extra probing calculations. In particular, we demonstrate the method for electron densities and nonlocal pseudopotential forces for fixed Kohn-Sham Hamiltonians of semiconductors, metals and thermally perturbed silica. The convergence is significantly accelerated by the spatial decay of the density matrix, especially if the density matrix is short-ranged. The number of probes necessary to...

items.title: Theoretical study of nitrogen-vacancy spin coherence enhanced by vacancy aggregation in diamond using cluster-correlation expansion
items.abstract: Annealing a semiconductor makes its vacancies mobile; they aggregate into multi-vacancy complexes that often carry spin. Such centres are a magnetic-noise source for any spin qubit among them, in silicon and silicon carbide as well as in diamond, and they are accordingly blamed for the decoherence of negatively charged nitrogen-vacancy (NV$^-$) centres in irradiated and implanted diamond, with two coherence records credited to removing them. Cluster-correlation-expansion simulations in which the spins outside each cluster keep exchanging spin projections in pairs reproduce the measured Hahn-echo coherence time of NV$^-$ centres in a substitutional-nitrogen bath to within 12%, inside the statistical uncertainty. Driven by published electron-paramagnetic-resonance parameters, the same calculation inverts the attribution. At a fixed paramagnetic spin density a multi-vacancy bath gives a Hah...

items.title: Uncertainty and Business-Aware Remaining Useful Life Estimation for Semiconductor Manufacturing
items.abstract: Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimates guide maintenance in semiconductor manufacturing, where a late intervention can disrupt production but an early one discards usable equipment life. A single prediction does not express the uncertainty needed to choose between these outcomes. We combine Deep Learning (DL) sequence models with Simoultaneous Quantile Regression (SQR) to estimate RUL at selectable quantile levels, and evaluate maintenance decisions using Unexpected Breaks (UB), Unexploited Lifetime (UL), and a cost-weighted objective. On the $F_1$ fault mode of the 2018 PHM Data Challenge (PHM18) ion-milling dataset, we compare recurrent, Transformer, and State Space Models (SSM) architectures. Diagonal State Spaced (S4D) gives the strongest overall RUL accuracy across the evaluated quantiles. Varying the quantile and maintenance window exposes the trade-off between failure risk and earl...

items.title: Transport-Noise and Optical Witnesses of Electronic Multipartite Entanglement
items.abstract: Entanglement among particles distinguishes correlated quantum materials from conventional metals and semiconductors. Experimentally certifying intrinsic entanglement among interacting electrons in materials is important not only for classifying states of matter, but also for developing material-based quantum technologies. Here, we introduce a transport protocol for witnessing multipartite entanglement from the equilibrium current-noise spectrum, measured directly or reconstructed from optical conductivity. The appropriately integrated, symmetrized, and projected noise spectrum obeys an upper bound derived from microscopic model parameters. Unlike witnesses based on localized spins, our framework applies to general electronic states without requiring magnetic moments and remains invariant under single-particle basis transformations. items.title: Who Needs DRAM? We Have Fiber
items.abstract: The rising pressure on DRAM availability and contract pricing reflects generative AI's massive high-performance memory requirements. This pressure is heavily compounded by hyperscale data center expansion, which now consumes a significant portion of global DRAM output. In this work, we propose a new architecture, Fiber Memory, which reimagines the role of optical fiber in a hyperscale data center, deploying it as an active, recirculating delay-line memory for immutable data, such as large language model weights. We present a hybrid data- and pipeline-parallel optical broadcast delay-line memory architecture that accounts for fiber's physical realities. By incorporating space-division multiplexed multi-core fibers, passive optical tap-and-amplify interfaces, co-packaged optics, and centralized in-ring 3R (re-amplify, reshape, retime) regeneration, our case study evaluation suggests that F...

items.title: Bright and Dark Excitons in CrSBr: Local Ligand-Field Character and Band-Coherent Optical Selection Rules
items.abstract: Magnetic van der Waals semiconductors such as CrSBr host an intricate exciton landscape. Quasiparticle self-consistent GW theory with electron-hole ladder vertex corrections (QSGWc) has established the gap and the character of the bright XA (1.34 eV) and XB (1.8 eV) excitons. Why these bright excitons coexist, within a few tens of meV, with companions orders of magnitude darker has remained unexplained. Here we show that brightness is fixed by a symmetry of the structure: a mirror-glide exchanges the two Cr atoms of each layer, every exciton has a definite parity under it, and bright and dark partners are its even and odd members. The even sector carries the b-axis dipole; the odd sector is suppressed by about three orders of magnitude. The dark partners of XA and XB occupy the same region of k-space as the bright states, and dark states such as the one at 1.50 eV are dipole-forbidden by...

items.title: Transmon Phase Gates Controlled by Superconducting Soliton DAC
items.abstract: We introduce a superconducting digital-to-analog converter (DAC) that filters control noise, provides native multiplexing, performs quantum gates in nanoseconds, and can be controlled by CMOS. This is achieved by transducing a trapezoidal drive pulse into a superconducting soliton, which is then held in the DAC load loop, applying flux to a mutually-coupled superconducting qubit or gate coupler. The analog flux output by the DAC can be easily controlled by varying the soliton hold time, or with a DC-biased tunable DAC-qubit coupler, allowing the DAC to perform a fixed-time, high-fidelity gate that's robust to fabrication variance or flux offsets in the quantum circuit. Our initial demonstration shows that the DAC can successfully perform 5.6 ns S-gates on transmons. We measure the DAC-induced quantum state excitation probability per gate to be 0.05%, and find that the DAC-induced relaxat...

items.title: Carruthers Data Processing Pipeline: Instrument Effect Correction
items.abstract: The Carruthers Geocorona Observatory -- launched in September 2025 -- is NASA's first mission devoted to investigating the fundamental nature of Earth's exosphere from its distant vantage in halo orbit around the Earth-Sun L1 Lagrange point. Its primary payload, the GeoCoronal Imager, consists of two coaligned photometric imagers that measure ultraviolet Lyman-alpha emission radiance from exospheric hydrogen simultaneously at wide- and narrow- fields of view. The imagers use MicroChannel Plate intensified Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor detectors, which are known to add various artifacts to the final image telemetered from the spacecraft, hereby known as instrument effects. This paper details the algorithms used to retrieve and remove instrument effects from raw telemetry on-orbit, including detector voltage bias, thermal dark current, particle radiation, flat-field, and distorti...

items.title: Controllable Quantum Spin Hall Phases in Bi$_2$Te$_3$-Family van der Waals Heterobilayers
items.abstract: The tunability and control of topological edge/surface states are crucial for the development of new device applications. In this work, by combining first-principles calculations and Wannier-based tight-binding methods, we show the emergence of quantum spin Hall phases in van der Waals heterostructures formed by stacking two trivial quintuple layers from the Bi$_2$Te$_3$ family. We demonstrate the tunability of the edge states under interlayer strain and external electric field effects, suggesting the possibility of switching topological edge states on/off by external control. Additionally, the quantum spin Hall edge channels remain robust against interlayer twist, highlighting their stability against external perturbations. Our results provide a new way to create and manipulate two-dimensional topological phases in systems based on Bi$_2$Te$_3$ family, which can be valuable for practica...

items.title: Coexistence of Donor and Acceptor Hydrogen States in n-Type InN
items.abstract: Hydrogen often exhibits amphoteric behavior in semiconductors, but its role is in n-type InN remains unresolved. Wurtzite InN is a narrow-gap semiconductor with high electron mobility and is therefore attractive for high-speed electronics and optoelectronic applications. Here we use hard x-ray photoemission spectroscopy (HAXPES) to probe hydrogen-related electronic structure in as-grown and post-annealed InN thin films prepared at different grown temperatures. Post annealing, which reduces the concentration of hydrogen impurities in the films, shifts the core-level spectra toward lower binding energy, consistent with a chemical-potential shift associated with the passivation of electron carriers. In the valence-band spectra, an acceptor-like in-gap feature near the valence-band maximum is suppressed after annealing. Together with the established donor-like behavior of hydrogen in InN, th...

items.title: Designing Strong and Broadband Nonreciprocal Thermal Radiation in Magnetic Topological Materials
items.abstract: Breaking reciprocity in thermal radiation opens opportunities for energy harvesting, sensing, and thermal management. Traditional nonreciprocal radiative semiconductor devices need external magnetic field. In this work, we predict a series of magnetic topological materials for magnetic-field-free nonreciprocal thermal radiation in the infrared regime, by combining first-principles calculations with Maxwell electrodynamics. We find strong and broadband nonreciprocity in magnetic Weyl semimetals (e.g., Co$_3$Sn$_2$S$_2$), outperforming the conventional semiconductor such as InAs. Furthermore, we propose universal material design recipes: strong nonreciprocity requires a large anomalous Hall response relative to the optical loss, whereas the broadband response favors large optical loss and small dielectric dispersion.
